properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 10 at 3:57PM EDT until October 11 at 6:00PM EDT by NWS Marquette MI
properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 002 Ontonagon and Fire
Weather Zone 009 Gogebic.

* TIMING...Until 6 PM EDT /5 PM CDT/ Sunday.

* WINDS...South 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 35 mph...diminishing
to 10 to 15 mph with gusts to 25 mph late tonight into Sunday.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 31 percent this
afternoon...recovering to 60 to 70 percent tonight. Sunday, as
low as 30 to 40 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures and
exceptionally dry fuels will create dangerous wildland fire
conditions. Campfires, outdoor grills, smoking materials,
fireworks, chain saws, and all-terrain vehicles all have the
potential to throw a spark and ignite a dangerous and destructive
fire.

cloud-to-ground lightning, and minor flooding due to heavy
rainfall.

properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes. If your vessel is
caught offshore, immediately secure for heavy weather. Ensure all
crew members are wearing USCG approved Type I life jackets and
nonessential crew are below decks. Deploy jack lines and harnesses if
available. Check life saving equipment, including batteries on
handheld radios, for readiness.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately. If your vessel is caught offshore, immediately secure
for heavy weather. Ensure all crew members are wearing USCG approved
Type I life jackets and nonessential crew are below decks. Deploy
jack lines and harnesses if available. Check life saving equipment,
including batteries on handheld radios, for readiness.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 10 at 1:38PM MDT until October 12 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Periods of heavy wet snow and blowing snow expected. Total
snow accumulations between 5 and 10 inches. Winds gusting as high
as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Melville Foothills.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to noon MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult on local roads and US-191
in the Melville vicinity. The hazardous conditions will impact the
Monday morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tree and power line damage is possible which
may result in power outages.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel be prepared for severe winter conditions. Keep an
extra flashlight, food, and water in your vehicle in case of an
emergency. For the latest road conditions, call 5 1 1.

accumulations between 2 and 6 inches with locally higher amounts
possible. Winds gusting as high as 40 mph.

* WHERE...Southern Wheatland, Beartooth Foothills, Livingston Area,
Northern Park, and Northern Sweet Grass.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to noon MDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult, due to areas of slushy or
snowy roads and poor visibility. This includes US-191 from Big

may result in power outages.
properties.instruction:

conditions, call 5 1 1.

caution while driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few
steps taken on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could
be icy and slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.
